US transit ridership identifies the public transit mode with the most reported annual unlinked boardings in an area. Use it when an agent needs the dominant observed local mode.
US transit mode availability reports the number of distinct providers for each mode in a US urban area. Use it when an agent needs the available categories of transit.
US transit agency operations list each mode and whether service is directly operated or contracted. Use it when an agent needs a specific operator’s service arrangements.
US transit providers by location return matching agencies, modes, IDs and an official verification link. Use it when an agent needs public transport providers for a US metro area.
Scheduled airport meeting access finds the scheduled airport minimizing the longer of two great-circle access distances. Use it when an agent needs a balanced arrival point between two locations.
Scheduled airport journey measurement returns the cumulative great-circle distance and longest leg for ordered IATA stops. Use it when an agent needs a distance estimate for a multi-stop itinerary.
Scheduled airport regions rank the subdivisions containing the most scheduled IATA airports in a country. Use it when an agent needs the regional distribution of passenger access.
Scheduled airport size mix counts large, medium, small and seaplane airports with scheduled service in a country. Use it when an agent needs a country airport inventory.
Scheduled airport catchment density counts passenger airports in consecutive distance bands around a coordinate. Use it when an agent needs the density of alternative airports.
Scheduled airport city search lists distinct IATA airports whose published municipality matches a location string. Use it when an agent needs the available arrival codes for a city.
Scheduled airport border comparison finds the nearest scheduled airport outside the named airport’s country. Use it when an agent needs an international arrival alternative.
Scheduled airport alternates return the nearest other scheduled airports in the same country as a named airport. Use it when an agent needs domestic alternative arrival points.
Scheduled airport lookup returns the municipality, country, region and reference coordinates for an IATA code. Use it when an agent needs a civil airport location.
Scheduled airport search returns nearby IATA airports in order of great-circle distance with optional radius and type. Use it when an agent needs a passenger airport near a destination.
Web Mercator latitude limits return the maximum north and south latitudes within a chosen spherical linear-scale inflation. Use it when an agent needs a validity band for a map tolerance.
Web Mercator segment measurement returns constant-bearing spherical rhumb distance and compass direction for two points. Use it when an agent needs a straight line in Mercator space.
Web Mercator pixel picking resolves a continuous raster edge coordinate within an explicitly stretched projected extent. Use it when an agent needs the geographic position of a selected image pixel.
Web Mercator area bias compares the projected rectangle area to the same meridian-parallel region on the reference sphere. Use it when an agent needs area inflation over an extent.
Web Mercator print framing returns the projected map scale denominator for a geographic area and paper dimensions. Use it when an agent needs the scale that fits a printed rectangle.
Web Mercator viewport fitting returns metres per pixel and unused horizontal or vertical canvas space. Use it when an agent needs a rectangular map fitted without cropping.
Web Mercator extent centres return the geographic point at the visual centre of a projected map window. Use it when an agent needs the centre of a framed map.
Web Mercator map envelopes split a crossing geographic extent into independent projected rectangles. Use it when an agent needs renderable extents on both sides of the date line.
Web Mercator inverse projection returns WGS84 longitude and latitude from map metres. Use it when an agent needs coordinates for a geographic interchange file.
Web Mercator forward projection returns EPSG:3857 easting and northing in metres from WGS84 longitude and latitude. Use it when an agent needs map coordinates for a geographic point.
Japan holiday comparison identifies uniquely named holidays whose month and day changed from the previous year. Use it when an agent needs annual schedule adjustments.
Japan holiday history finds the official dates of a named holiday in a bounded year window. Use it when an agent needs the observed dates of a specific Japanese holiday.
Japan calendar closures return the longest continuous run of weekends and statutory holidays in a range. Use it when an agent needs the longest interruption to weekday schedules.
Japan working-day offsets return the date reached by moving a signed number of working days from an anchor. Use it when an agent needs a due date on the Japanese business calendar.
Japan business days return the inclusive count of weekdays excluding official national holidays. Use it when an agent needs settlement or delivery planning.
Japan holiday lookup reports the statutory label and weekday for a specified civil date. Use it when an agent needs a Japanese holiday status check.
Japan national holidays return the official dates and Japanese names for a selected year. Use it when an agent needs the Cabinet Office annual holiday list.
Station frequency shift compares scheduled departure counts before and after the window midpoint. Use it when an agent needs a near-term increase or drop in trip supply.
Station clockface timing returns the most frequent departure phase relative to a chosen periodic grid. Use it when an agent needs a timetable pulse offset.
Station departure regularity returns the root mean square change between successive distinct departure gaps. Use it when an agent needs a schedule regularity metric.
Station departure density returns scheduled trip counts in consecutive five-minute bins anchored at the requested start. Use it when an agent needs short platform demand windows.
Station transfer locations count eligible connections at the same GTFS stop ID and at different station members. Use it when an agent needs a same-platform-stop proxy.
Station transfer coverage counts arriving services with a different onward route within thirty minutes. Use it when an agent needs the number of arrivals with an onward option.
Transit loop analysis returns repeat visits to the same stop and the shortest interval until a revisit. Use it when an agent needs repeat-stop evidence in a trip segment.
Transit schedule recovery returns accumulated intermediate dwell above a minimum retained hold. Use it when an agent needs a bounded timetable recovery estimate.
Transit connection time returns transfer slack after a supplied minimum connection time. Use it when an agent needs the margin between an incoming service and an outgoing stop.
Transit overnight travel returns scheduled seconds before and after service-day midnight. Use it when an agent needs to allocate overnight travel to calendar days.
Transit stop frequency returns the busiest half-open departure window within a single trip. Use it when an agent needs the densest section of a timetable.
Transit dwell time returns the longest intermediate stop and its scheduled holding seconds. Use it when an agent needs the longest scheduled pause excluding terminal time.
Transit travel time returns the longest uninterrupted run between consecutive stops. Use it when an agent needs the maximum stop-to-stop running time.
Transit boarding eligibility returns pickup and drop-off conditions for a proposed stop pair. Use it when an agent needs to check whether a scheduled boarding pair requires prior arrangements.
Transit trip position returns the scheduled stop or pair of stops at a service-day time. Use it when an agent needs a timetable position at a given instant.
Transit travel time returns moving and intermediate dwell seconds in a scheduled trip segment. Use it when an agent needs a scheduled travel time breakdown.
Local time sequence auditing returns adjacent chronological events whose local wall clocks move backward. Use it when an agent needs to detect local time ordering errors in an event log.
Regional shift overlap returns the concurrent UTC interval of two shifts expressed in different local clocks. Use it when an agent needs to measure staffed coverage across offices.
Quarter-hour scheduling returns the next observable local clock quarter and its UTC instant. Use it when an agent needs to align a job to a local quarter-hour across offset changes.
Timezone offset validation returns whether the numeric offset in a timestamp matches the zone at that instant. Use it when an agent needs to validate time-stamped business records.

Recurring meeting time returns the change in UTC hour between weekly occurrences held at the same local time. Use it when an agent needs to identify calendar series that shift for international attend
Timezone convert returns local clocks, offsets, weekdays and abbreviations at one instant for up to ten destinations. Use it when an agent needs to schedule a call across cities.
Marine weather bulletins return the official German coastal or sea-area forecast. Use it when an agent needs an area-based DWD report. © Deutscher Wetterdienst.
Antimeridian crossing returns the latitude and along-leg distance where a WGS84 segment crosses the date line. Use it when an agent needs to split a geodesic for a map projection.
Geodesic projection returns the nearest regional leg point and its distance. Use it when an agent needs a nearest station on a regional segment.
Route geometry returns the sum of ellipsoid legs, endpoint distance and excess distance via the waypoints. Use it when an agent needs to quantify indirectness in a supplied itinerary.
Geodesic waypoint returns the coordinate at a requested along-track distance on a bounded leg. Use it when an agent needs to locate a station between surveyed endpoints.
Map tile area returns the tile’s spherical surface area and its fraction of the sphere. Use it when an agent needs to area-weight a tile grid.
Map tile neighbors return distinct edge-adjacent XYZ tiles with longitude wrapping. Use it when an agent needs to prefetch adjacent map tiles.
Map quadkeys return the rectangular range and count of descendants at a target zoom. Use it when an agent needs to fetch a subtree of a tile index.
Map point grouping returns the deepest XYZ tile shared by two coordinates through zoom 22. Use it when an agent needs to group two points in a tile pyramid.
Map tile budgeting returns the highest zoom whose complete viewport fits a tile-count budget. Use it when an agent needs to cap offline map size.
Map viewport coverage returns compact XYZ tile ranges including antimeridian-crossing boxes. Use it when an agent needs to enumerate tiles for a viewport.
Map resolution returns local ground meters per pixel and nominal ground width of a tile at latitude. Use it when an agent needs to choose a zoom for a required map resolution.
Map tile bounds return the geographic west, south, east and north edges of an XYZ tile. Use it when an agent needs to cut data to tile boundaries.
Map tiles return the XYZ tile and pixel containing a geographic coordinate. Use it when an agent needs to place a marker on a raster tile.
